subject: Climate & Environment
title: Cattle Ranching and the Amazon
description: Learn Cattle Ranching and the Amazon in one minute.

hook.text: About 80% of Amazon deforestation is driven by one industry: cattle ranching.

buildup.text: Ranchers clear forest with fire, plant grass, and graze cattle for a few years.

discovery.text: The soil is thin and nutrient-poor. After a few years, ranchers move on and clear more.

twist.text: Much of this beef is exported to feed demand in Europe, China, and the Middle East.

climax.text: A single hamburger from deforested land costs roughly 6.5 square meters of rainforest.

punchline.text: The world's appetite for beef is eating the Amazon.

quiz.question: What is the leading cause of Amazon deforestation?

details.summary: Cattle ranching is the single largest driver of Amazon deforestation, responsible for roughly 80 percent of cleared forest. Land is burned to create pasture for beef cattle, much of which is exported to global markets through supply chains that are difficult to trace.
details.whyItMatters: The global appetite for beef directly drives tropical forest destruction. Supply chain transparency is essential to breaking the link between hamburgers and deforestation.
takeaways: Cattle ranching causes about 80 percent of Amazon deforestation
Brazil is the world's largest beef exporter
Many companies cannot trace beef back to the ranch of origin

faq.question: Why is cattle ranching so dominant in Amazon deforestation?
faq.answer: Cattle ranching is low-cost, requires little labor, and serves as a tool for land speculation. Clearing forest and placing cattle establishes a legal land claim, making ranching as much about property value as beef production.

faq.question: Can sustainable beef reduce Amazon deforestation?
faq.answer: Intensifying production on existing pasture could meet demand without new clearing. However, enforcement is weak, laundering cattle through compliant ranches is common, and economic incentives still favor expansion over intensification.
